mentions.name: EACL (Enterprise Access ControL)
mentions.description: EACL (Enterprise Access ControL) is a situated ReBAC authorization library inspired by SpiceDB, built in Clojure and backed by Datomic Pro, Datahike, Datalevin, or DataScript. Permissions are stored as data that co-exist with the application's data, which provides reduced network latency, strong local consistency, and opportunities for real-time view maintenance. It ships with a performance demo (1M permissioned entities, 3.8M relationships), an in-browser toy Google Drive clone, and handles authorization in the Datahike HTTP server; EACL V8 RC was released to Clojars.

mentions.name: EACL (Enterprise Access ControL)
mentions.description: This is a situated ReBAC (relationship-based access control) authorization system based on SpiceDB, built in Clojure and backed by Datomic. Permission schemas and permission data live alongside the application's data, eliminating a network hop, a distributed consistency/syncing problem, and an extra component to run in production versus external authorization services. It can implement ZedToken/Zookies-style consistency via Datomic transaction IDs, is fast without a cache because horizontally-scalable Datomic Peers aggressively cache datoms (with another 10-100x improvement planned), supports easy schema testing with in-memory Datomic, and is especially suitable for real-time multiplayer apps built with frameworks like Electric Clojure. ReBAC subsumes both ABAC and RBAC.
mentions.problem: External authorization services like SpiceDB add extra network hops, distributed consistency/syncing overhead, and another component to run in production; intermediate resource traversal cursors are the primary performance bottleneck the author is working to improve.
mentions.audience: Clojure developers building applications, especially real-time multiplayer apps
